correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge3\), \(B>0\), and \(t>0\), the hub-versus-rim and mean first-Fourier Rayleigh quotients bound \(\lambda_2\) by the minimum of two affine functions of total rim conductance. Exact maximization yields the three cases. The Fourier wheel spectrum achieves each bound, including equality thresholds. Crucially, equality in the mean Fourier bound forces both real Fourier vectors to be eigenvectors; taking the imaginary part of the resulting complex eigen-equation forces all rim weights equal because \(\sin(2\pi/n)\) is nonzero, then all spokes equal. No unstated symmetry hypothesis. Exact-rational critical cases and 2141 symbolic/numerical assertions corroborate; finite tests are not used to prove the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The answer is an exact natural complete classification for freely weighted wheels, including every optimizer rather than one symmetric representative. It has an exact support-deletion boundary shrinking as \(4\pi^2/n^2\), with a one-dimensional nonunique optimal face precisely at the price tie. Rigidity excludes all asymmetric optimizers, a property not established merely by group averaging. The threshold and flat face have direct relevance to network diffusion-rate design; the result is not claimed as a general spectral graph theorem or merely as a numerical gain.
